'''Rebecca Cooke''' (born December 21, 1987) is an American politician, nonprofit founder, and former political consultant who is the [[U.S. representative]]-elect for {{ushr|WI|3}}. A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]], Cooke defeated [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Derrick Van Orden]] in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Wisconsin#District 3|2026 election]] after unsuccessfully running in [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Wisconsin#District 3|2022]] and [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Wisconsin#District 3|2024]]. From 2019 to 2021, Cooke served on the board of the [[Wisconsin Economic Development Corporation]].

== Early life and education ==
Rebecca Cooke was born on December 21, 1987,<ref>{{cite web |title=2024 Wisconsin Election Guide |url=https://www.wispolitics.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/2024WisconsinElectionGuide.pdf |website=WisPolitics |access-date=31 May 2026 |quote=Rebecca Cooke (D) Born Dec. 21, 1987, in Eau Claire.}}</ref> in [[Eau Claire, Wisconsin|Eau Claire]], [[Wisconsin]],<ref name="Pierce">{{cite web |last1=Nigbor |first1=Sarah |title=Wisconsin Congressional District 3: Rebecca Cooke vs. Derrick Van Orden |url=https://www.piercecountyjournal.news/stories/wisconsin-congressional-district-3-rebecca-cooke-vs-derrick-van-orden,111158 |website=Pierce County Journal |access-date=31 May 2026 |language=en |date=30 October 2024}}</ref> the youngest of three children in a [[dairy farming]] family.<ref name="Meet">{{cite web |title=Meet Rebecca Cooke |url=https://cookeforwisconsin.com/meet-rebecca-cooke/ |website=Cooke for Wisconsin |access-date=31 May 2026}}</ref><ref name="Cap">{{cite web |last1=Nichols |first1=John |title=Rebecca Cooke's campaign is rooted in Wisconsin history |url=https://captimes.com/opinion/john-nichols/opinion-rebecca-cooke-s-campaign-is-rooted-in-wisconsin-history/article_0943141a-79ed-11ef-9395-6f03a61e3318.html |website=The Cap Times |access-date=31 May 2026 |language=en |date=24 September 2024}}</ref> She is a descendant of abolitionist [[Chauncey H. Cooke|Chauncey Cooke]].<ref name="Pierce"/>

Cooke attended [[4-H]] youth programs as a child,<ref>{{cite web |title=4-H |url=https://awpc.cattcenter.iastate.edu/communication/4-h-jul-29-2024 |website=Iowa State University Archives of Women's Political Communication |access-date=31 May 2026}}</ref> and was the president of her local 4-H club.<ref name="WPo">{{cite web |title=This rising House Democrat is a voice for the angry middle |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2025/11/13/democrat-jason-crow-midterms-veterans-colorado/ |website=The Washington Post |access-date=1 June 2026 |language=en |date=13 November 2025 |quote=Rebecca Cooke, 38, the waitress from Eau Claire, Wisconsin, told me that the first office she ever held was president of her 4-H club.}}</ref> She began waitressing at 16 while attending [[North High School (Eau Claire, Wisconsin)|North High School]].<ref name="Guardian">{{cite web |last1=Leingang |first1=Rachel |title=She's a waitress raised on a farm – can Rebecca Cooke win a key Wisconsin seat? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/apr/04/rebecca-cooke-democrat-wisconsin-race |website=The Guardian |access-date=31 May 2026 |date=4 April 2025}}</ref><ref name="Thirdnew"/> After graduating, Cooke earned a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree from the [[University of St. Thomas (Minnesota)|University of St. Thomas]].<ref name="Stevens">{{cite web |last1=Pfantz |first1=Erik |title=Meet the candidates running for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District seat |url=https://www.stevenspointjournal.com/story/news/politics/elections/2024/09/18/who-is-running-for-wisconsins-3rd-congressional-district-seat/75193822007/ |website=Stevens Point Journal |access-date=31 May 2026}}</ref>

== Career ==
After college, Cooke worked as a fundraiser for national campaigns. From 2012 to 2014, she served as finance director for four congressional campaigns in four U.S. states.<ref name="Outsider">{{cite web |last1=Bice |first1=Daniel |title=Cooke says she's a political outsider but raked in nearly $200K for political work |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/news/politics/elections/2024/07/25/rebecca-cooke-says-shes-an-outsider-but-raked-in-consulting-cash/74516932007/ |website=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel |access-date=31 May 2026}}</ref><ref name="BergeJ">{{cite web |last=Schulte |first=Laura |date=April 20, 2026 |title=GOP, Dem challenger hit Rebecca Cooke for outside political work |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/news/politics/2026/04/16/gop-dem-challenger-hit-rebecca-cooke-for-outside-political-work/89181656007/ |website=Journal Sentinel |access-date=31 May 2026}}</ref> In 2014,<ref name="Colfax"/> she moved back to Eau Claire, where she opened a home goods store, Red's Mercantile,<ref name="WPR">{{cite web |title=Eau Claire business owner Rebecca Cooke launches run for 3rd Congressional District seat |url=https://www.wpr.org/politics/eau-claire-business-owner-rebecca-cooke-launches-run-3rd-congressional-district-seat |website=WPR |access-date=31 May 2026 |date=13 October 2021}}</ref> and began to work as a political consultant. Between 2015 and 2021, Cooke's consulting firm advised eight political campaigns.<ref name="Outsider"/><ref name="BergeJ"/>

In 2016, Cooke founded a nonprofit to support female business owners with grants.<ref name="Outsider"/> In 2019, Governor [[Tony Evers]] appointed her to the [[Wisconsin Economic Development Corporation]]'s board of directors,<ref>{{cite web |title=WEDC names members of new Entrepreneurship and Innovation Committee |url=https://dailyreporter.com/2019/09/11/wedc-names-members-of-new-entrepreneurship-and-innovation-committee/ |website=The Daily Reporter |access-date=31 May 2026 |date=11 September 2019}}</ref><ref name="WPR"/> where she co-chaired the Entrepreneurship & Innovation Committee and later served as board secretary.<ref name="Pierce"/> Cooke resigned from the board in November 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=Press Release: Gov. Evers Appoints Jack Salzwedel to the WEDC Board of Directors |url=https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/WIGOV/bulletins/2fe5d14 |website=State of Wisconsin |access-date=31 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref> In 2022, she closed her home goods store.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Scherer |first1=McKenna |title=One Door Closes, Another Opens: Red's Says Goodbye, Menomonie Shop Moving In |url=https://volumeone.org/articles/2022/08/19/302792-when-one-door-closes-another-opens-reds |website=Volume One |access-date=31 May 2026 |language=en |date=19 August 2022}}</ref><ref name="Spec">{{cite web |title=Democrat challenges Rep. Van Orden in Wisconsin battleground |url=https://spectrumnews1.com/wi/milwaukee/news/2023/07/10/democrat-rebecca-cooke--challenges--van-orden--wisconsin- |website=Spectrum News |access-date=31 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref> Until 2025, Cooke ran a consulting company advising small businesses.<ref name="Thirdnew"/>

== Congressional campaigns ==
=== 2022 ===
{{Main|2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Wisconsin#District 3|l1 = 2022 Wisconsin's 3rd congressional district election}}

Cooke sought to represent [[Wisconsin's 3rd congressional district]] in 2022, coming second in the Democratic primary to state senator [[Brad Pfaff]].<ref name="News8000">{{cite web |last1=Israr |first1=Duaa |title=An underdog rises: Rebecca Cooke's loss is a win for rural votes in Wisconsin |url=https://www.news8000.com/news/politics/elections/an-underdog-rises-rebecca-cooke-s-loss-is-a-win-for-rural-votes-in-wisconsin/article_48a13c9f-c915-5ff9-b6eb-be25718c8683.html |website=News8000 |access-date=31 May 2026 |language=en |date=10 August 2022}}</ref> Running as a [[Blue Dog Coalition|Blue Dog Democrat]],<ref name="NewYorker" /><ref name="Guardian" /><ref name="Mother">{{cite web |last1=Lanard |first1=Noah |title=Can a waitress running on economic populism beat a MAGA Republican who yells at teens? |url=https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2024/11/rebecca-cooke-van-orden-swing-district-wisconsin-blue-dog-democrat/ |website=Mother Jones |access-date=31 May 2026}}</ref> Cooke campaigned on improving the economy, lowering healthcare costs, and investing in infrastructure.<ref name="WPR" /> She lost by seven points in what was called an underdog campaign. She performed best in the district's rural areas.<ref name="News8000" />

=== 2024 ===
{{Main|2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Wisconsin#District 3|l1 = 2024 Wisconsin's 3rd congressional district election}}

Cooke ran to represent the 3rd congressional district again while continuing to work three nights a week as a waitress.<ref name="Mother"/><ref name="Urban">{{cite web |last1=Redman |first1=Henry |title=Rebecca Cooke Believes She Can Turn 3rd Congressional District Blue |url=https://urbanmilwaukee.com/2024/03/25/rebecca-cooke-believes-she-can-turn-3rd-congressional-district-blue/ |website=Urban Milwaukee |access-date=31 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref> She campaigned as a moderate Democrat,<ref>{{cite web |title=Democrat Rebecca Cooke considers another congressional run after outpacing Harris, Baldwin |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/news/politics/elections/2024/12/10/rebecca-cooke-considers-another-run-after-outpacing-harris-baldwin/76739028007/ |website=Journal Sentinel |access-date=31 May 2026 |quote=And in Washington, several congressional Democrats praised the campaign from Cooke, who ran as a moderate Democrat in the purple district.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Andrea |first1=Lawrence |title=Democrat Rebecca Cooke launches bid to unseat Derrick Van Orden in Wisconsin battleground seat |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/news/politics/elections/2025/03/11/democrat-rebecca-cooke-launches-bid-to-unseat-derrick-van-orden/82225312007/ |website=Journal Sentinel |access-date=31 May 2026}}</ref> and pledged to join the centrist [[Blue Dog Coalition]] if elected,<ref name="PolBlue">{{cite web |last1=Fertig |first1=Natalie |title=Blue Dogs aim to grow their ranks |url=https://www.politico.com/newsletters/politico-nightly/2024/08/14/blue-dogs-aim-to-grow-their-ranks-00174072 |website=POLITICO |access-date=31 May 2026 |language=en |date=14 August 2024 |quote=But if she wins, she plans to join the Blue Dog Coalition currently co-chaired by Golden and Gluesenkamp Perez.}}</ref><ref name="Examiner">{{cite web |last1=Redman |first1=Henry |title=Rebecca Cooke believes her 'working class' values can flip 3rd Congressional District blue |url=https://wisconsinexaminer.com/2024/03/20/rebecca-cooke-believes-her-working-class-values-can-flip-3rd-congressional-district-blue/ |website=Wisconsin Examiner |access-date=31 May 2026 |date=20 March 2024}}</ref> though she emphasized her support for abortion rights and healthcare reform.<ref name="Examiner"/> ''[[Mother Jones (magazine)|Mother Jones]]'' called Cooke's campaign style "a moderate version of Democratic populism".<ref name="Mother"/>

[[File:Rebecca Cooke being interviewed by UpNorthNews August 2025 (cropped).jpg|thumb|230x230px|Cooke being interviewed by ''UpNorthNews'' in August 2025]]

The incumbent, [[Derrick Van Orden]], defeated Cooke in the general election by less than three points.<ref>{{cite web |title=Milk's the drink of choice at RFK Jr.'s event with swing-district Republican |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/01/rfk-van-orden-wisconsin-milk-00945679 |website=POLITICO |access-date=2 June 2026 |language=en |date=1 June 2026 |quote=The Democrat [Van Orden] defeated two years ago by less than 3 points, Rebecca Cooke, is the daughter of a dairy farmer who has run a small business and a nonprofit supporting women entrepreneurs.}}</ref><ref name="Nineteenth">{{cite web |last1=Panetta |first1=Grace |title=In rural Wisconsin, politics is still about meeting voters. Online, it's getting weird. |url=https://19thnews.org/2026/10/rebecca-cooke-wisconsin-house-campaign/ |website=The 19th |access-date=8 October 2026 |language=en-us |date=5 October 2026}}</ref> She outperformed [[Kamala Harris]] in the concurrently held [[2024 United States presidential election in Wisconsin|presidential election]].<ref name="NewYorker">{{cite web |last1=Slevin |first1=Peter |title=How Much Do Democrats Need to Change? |url=https://www.newyorker.com/news/the-lede/how-much-do-democrats-need-to-change |website=The New Yorker |access-date=31 May 2026 |date=30 December 2024}}</ref><ref name="NYT"/>

=== 2026 ===
{{Main|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Wisconsin#District 3|l1 = 2026 Wisconsin's 3rd congressional district election}}

Cooke was the Democratic nominee in the 2026 election for the 3rd congressional district.<ref name="NYT">{{cite web |last1=Karni |first1=Annie |title=In the Battle for Congress, Working-Class Democrats Try a Hardscrabble Pitch |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/07/us/politics/in-the-battle-for-congress-working-class-democrats-try-a-hardscrabble-pitch.html |website=The New York Times |access-date=31 May 2026 |date=7 September 2025 |quote=Some of the current crop of working-class candidates are running again after coming close two years ago. Ms. Cooke ran for Congress in 2024 and lost to Mr. Van Orden by less than 3 percentage points. She outperformed Ms. Harris by roughly 9,000 votes and Senator Tammy Baldwin, a Democrat, by about 5,000 votes in a southwestern Wisconsin district that includes Eau Claire.}}</ref> Considered the front-runner in the Democratic primary,<ref name="BergeJ"/> she received "a wide range of Democratic endorsements from progressives and moderates",<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gans |first1=Jared |title=Sanders wades into battleground district with Wisconsin endorsement |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5359217-bernie-sanders-endorsement-wisconsin-rebecca-cooke/ |website=The Hill |access-date=31 May 2026 |date=19 June 2025}}</ref> earning the support of [[Bernie Sanders]] as well as the [[New Democrat Coalition]] and the Blue Dog Caucus.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Razor |first1=Calen |last2=Mccarthy |first2=Mia |last3=Guggenheim |first3=Benjamin |title=A tough week for Susan Collins |url=https://www.politico.com/newsletters/inside-congress/2025/07/14/a-tough-week-for-susan-collins-00450745 |website=POLITICO |access-date=31 May 2026 |language=en |date=14 July 2025 |quote=The New Democrat Coalition’s political arm is endorsing its first slate of candidates for the 2026 midterms...The centrist bloc is backing ... Rebecca Cooke in Wisconsin's 3rd District}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=John |first1=Arit |title=Democrats want to win back Congress. First they need to weather their primary battles |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2025/12/13/politics/democratic-primaries-justice-democrats |website=CNN |access-date=31 May 2026 |language=en |date=13 December 2025 |quote=At times, the factions within the party have aligned behind a candidate. Sanders, Welcome PAC and the moderate Blue Dog wing of the party have all endorsed Wisconsin Democrat Rebecca Cooke, who narrowly lost her 2024 bid to unseat Republican Rep. Derrick Van Orden.}}</ref> 

Prior to the August 11 Democratic primary,<ref name="Win2026Primary">{{cite web |last1=Liederman |first1=Mack |title=Rebecca Cooke Wins Democratic Primary for Key Wisconsin House Seat |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/11/us/politics/wisconsin-democratic-primary-berge-cooke.html |website=The New York Times |access-date=12 August 2026 |date=12 August 2026}}</ref> Cooke confirmed that this would be her last campaign for the seat if she did not win.<ref>{{cite web |title=Biden's transportation secretary endorses Rebecca Cooke |url=https://spectrumnews1.com/wi/milwaukee/news/2026/02/09/rebecca-cooke--pete-buttigieg--endorsement |website=Spectrum News |access-date=31 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Cooke running for third and final time for Congress |url=https://spectrumnews1.com/wi/milwaukee/news/2025/04/07/cooke-van-orden-wisconsin-third |website=Spectrum News |access-date=31 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref> After becoming her party's nominee, Cooke was described by the libertarian magazine ''[[Reason (magazine)|Reason]]'' as "a straight shooter in a district that probably needs that type of candidate".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wolfe |first1=Liz |title=Hong's swan song |url=https://reason.com/2026/08/12/hongs-swan-song/ |website=Reason |access-date=13 August 2026 |date=12 August 2026}}</ref> She defeated Van Orden by roughly seven percentage points in the November 3 general election.<ref name="2026ElectionNBC">{{cite web |title=Wisconsin House District 3 Midterm Election 2026: Live Results |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/wisconsin-us-house-district-3-results |website=NBC News |access-date=4 November 2026 |language=en |date=4 November 2026}}</ref>

== Political views ==
Cooke identifies as a [[Centrism|centrist]],<ref name="Centrist">{{cite web |title=3rd Congressional District Democrats say they'll represent regular people better than Van Orden |url=https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/3rd-congressional-district-democrats-say-theyll-represent-regular-people-better-van-orden |website=News From The States |access-date=1 June 2026 |language=en}}</ref> and has repeatedly said she plans to caucus with the [[Blue Dog Coalition|Blue Dogs]] if elected.<ref name="PolBlue"/><ref name="Examiner"/><ref name="Very">{{cite web |title=Bernie Sanders dives into a key House battleground Trump carried in 2024 with a new endorsement |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/bernie-sanders-dives-key-house-battleground-trump-carried-2024-new-end-rcna213874 |website=NBC News |access-date=31 May 2026 |language=en |date=19 June 2025}}</ref> Speaking to ''[[Politico]]'', she said she does "not identify as a progressive".<ref name="Thirdnew"/> Cooke has criticized the national Democratic Party's public image,<ref name="NewYorker"/> calling their branding "far left" and out of touch with most Americans.<ref name="NewYorker"/> She has called congressional Democrats "too far left" and congressional Republicans "too far right".<ref name="Mother"/>

Cooke has opposed calls to [[defund the police]] and [[abolish ICE]].<ref name="Abolish">{{cite web |last1=Redman |first1=Henry |title=Former Eau Claire Council President Emily Berge's insurgent campaign in the 3rd CD |url=https://wisconsinexaminer.com/2026/07/22/former-eau-claire-common-council-president-berges-insurgent-campaign-in-the-3rd-cd/ |website=Wisconsin Examiner |access-date=25 July 2026 |date=22 July 2026}}</ref> She supports [[universal background check]]s and stronger enforcement of [[red flag laws]].<ref name="PolBlue"/> Cooke is [[pro-choice]] and has called abortion a decision that should be "free from political or governmental interference".<ref name= "Mother" />

Cooke opposes [[Medicare for All]],<ref name="Thirdnew"/> instead supporting the expansion of [[Medicare (United States)|Medicare]] to cover dental, hearing, and vision.<ref name= "Centrist" /> She has backed stronger [[United States antitrust law|antitrust laws]],<ref name= "Mother"/> and supports increasing the minimum wage to $15.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kreitlow |first1=Pat |title=How do Van Orden and Cooke compare on economic issues? |url=https://upnorthnewswi.com/news/politics/cooke-van-orden-economic-plans/ |website=UpNorthNews |access-date=4 November 2026 |date=17 September 2026}}</ref>

Cooke supported the [[2026 United States intervention in Venezuela]] and the ouster of President [[Nicolás Maduro]], but criticized the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]]'s lack of a "concrete plan for stability" in the country.<ref name="Venezuela">{{cite web |last1=Redman |first1=Henry |title=Venezuelan military action divides Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District candidates |url=https://wisconsinexaminer.com/2026/01/08/venezuelan-military-action-divides-wisconsins-3rd-congressional-district-candidates/ |website=Wisconsin Examiner |access-date=5 June 2026 |date=8 January 2026}}</ref> She has opposed [[foreign ownership]] of American farmland,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Styf |first1=Jon |title=Wisconsin 3rd Congressional race has focus on Chinese connections |url=https://www.thecentersquare.com/wisconsin/article_98fbb3cc-3067-44f7-86b2-19510509900c.html |website=The Center Square |access-date=5 June 2026 |language=en |date=3 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Schnitz |first1=Kelsey |title=Rebecca Cooke spoke at family farm ahead of presidential visit in Chippewa Falls |url=https://www.wsaw.com/2026/06/05/rebecca-cooke-spoke-family-farm-ahead-presidential-visit-chippewa-falls/ |website=WSAW |language=en |date=5 June 2026 |quote=Cooke is calling for...protections on American farmland from foreign buyers}}</ref> and criticized [[Tariffs in the second Trump administration|tariffs imposed by the Trump administration]] for causing family farm bankruptcies.<ref name="FarmCountry">{{cite web |title=Farm country loves Trump. His policies are making life difficult for this ally. |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/05/trump-campaign-vulnerable-house-republican-wisconsin-race-00950981 |website=POLITICO |access-date=6 June 2026 |language=en |date=5 June 2026}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Cooke lives in a "small, rundown house" on [[Tainter Lake]] in [[Colfax, Wisconsin]].<ref name="Thirdnew"/><ref name="Colfax">{{cite web |last1=Pfantz |first1=Erik |title=Meet the Democratic candidates for 3rd Congressional District seat |url=https://www.stevenspointjournal.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/07/28/meet-the-democratic-candidates-for-wisconsin-3rd-congressional-district-seat-august-11-primary/91013180007/ |website=Stevens Point Journal |access-date=30 July 2026}}</ref> She is a personal friend of U.S. representative [[Marie Gluesenkamp Perez]], the co-chair of the Blue Dog Coalition.<ref name="Mother"/><ref name="Thirdnew"/> Cooke is [[Protestantism in the United States|Protestant]].<ref name="Ballot">{{cite web |title=Rebecca Cooke |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Rebecca_Cooke |website=Ballotpedia |access-date=31 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref> Until 2025, she had a [[fellowship]] with the centrist think tank [[Third Way]].<ref name="Thirdnew">{{cite web |title=The Democratic Civil War Is Raging — Except in This Swing-State Race |url=https://www.politico.com/news/magazine/2026/10/04/rebecca-cooke-wisconsin-midterms-democrats-01097477 |website=POLITICO |access-date=8 October 2026 |language=en |date=4 October 2026}}</ref>
